title: Karl Counter-Argument: Universal healthcare means long waits
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Universal healthcare means long waits]

Americans wait too: for approvals, specialist appointments, and coverage decisions. Many countries with universal systems match or beat the U.S. on timely access. And millions here wait forever because they can't afford care at all.

[Sources: Commonwealth Fund Mirror, Mirror 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Single payer means death panels
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Single payer means death panels]

Private insurers already deny claims. On the ACA marketplace about 17% of in-network claims were denied in 2021. The rationing exists now. It's just done for profit.

[Sources: KFF 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Climate policy hurts the poor
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Climate policy hurts the poor]

Climate change hurts the poor most. Policies like carbon dividends, public transit, home weatherization and clean energy jobs can leave low-income families better off.

[Sources: IPCC AR6, Resources for the Future]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Renewable energy is unreliable
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Renewable energy is unreliable]

Grids from Texas to California have added massive amounts of solar, wind and batteries. Batteries and better transmission handle the variability. Fossil plants failed badly during Texas's 2021 winter blackout.

[Sources: ERCOT, FERC/NERC Winter Storm Uri report 2021]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Electric cars are worse for the environment
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Electric cars are worse for the environment]

Lifecycle studies find battery-electric cars produce far lower emissions than gas cars over their life, even counting battery manufacturing, and the gap grows as grids get cleaner.

[Sources: ICCT 2021]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Why should we act when China pollutes more?
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Why should we act when China pollutes more?]

The U.S. has put more cumulative carbon dioxide in the atmosphere than any other country, and Americans emit far more per person than the Chinese. We have the money and responsibility to lead.

[Sources: Carbon Brief 2021, Global Carbon Project]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Systemic racism doesn't exist
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Systemic racism doesn't exist]

Measured outcomes say otherwise: the median white family has roughly six times the wealth of the median Black family, Black mothers die at more than twice the rate, and Black Americans are arrested for marijuana at far higher rates despite similar usage.

[Sources: Federal Reserve SCF 2022, CDC 2022, ACLU 2020]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Slavery was a long time ago
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Slavery was a long time ago]

Redlining, legal segregation, and exclusion from New Deal programs happened in living memory. Those policies shaped who could buy homes and build wealth, and that wealth passed down.

[Sources: Rothstein, The Color of Law, Katznelson, When Affirmative Action Was White]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Reparations are impossible
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Reparations are impossible]

The U.S. paid reparations to Japanese Americans incarcerated during WWII through the Civil Liberties Act of 1988. Germany has paid reparations to Holocaust survivors for decades. It's a question of will.

[Sources: Civil Liberties Act of 1988]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Crime is skyrocketing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Crime is skyrocketing]

Murders fell sharply in 2023 and 2024, among the largest declines on record. Violent crime is far below its early-1990s peak.

[Sources: FBI UCR, Council on Criminal Justice]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Homeless people choose to live on the street
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Homeless people choose to live on the street]

Homelessness rates track housing costs, not personal choices. When cities offer real housing instead of shelters with strict rules, most people accept it.

[Sources: Colburn & Aldern 2022, HUD]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Housing First doesn't work
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Housing First doesn't work]

Houston cut homelessness by more than half after adopting Housing First. Research shows it keeps most people stably housed.

[Sources: Coalition for the Homeless Houston, HUD research]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Mutual aid is just charity
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Mutual aid is just charity]

Charity flows from the rich down with conditions attached. Mutual aid is people with shared problems helping each other as equals, and it often builds the relationships that turn into organizing.

[Sources: Spade, Mutual Aid 2020]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Strikes hurt the economy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Strikes hurt the economy]

Short-term disruption buys long-term gains: higher wages that workers spend in their communities. The economy belongs to the people doing the work, not the other way around.

[Sources: BLS Major Work Stoppages, EPI]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Union bosses just get rich off dues
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Union bosses just get rich off dues]

Union officers are elected by members, and finances are disclosed to the Department of Labor. Compare that to CEOs who make roughly 290 times their workers' pay with no vote from workers at all.

[Sources: DOL Office of Labor-Management Standards, EPI 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Unions protect bad workers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Unions protect bad workers]

Unions guarantee due process, not jobs. A worker gets a fair hearing before being fired. Without a union, most workers can be fired for almost any reason.

[Sources: NLRB, At-will employment law]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Billionaires give back through philanthropy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Billionaires give back through philanthropy]

Philanthropy is tax-advantaged and lets billionaires decide public priorities without voting. Many pledges move slowly, and foundations can hold wealth for generations. Democracy should decide public needs, not donors.

[Sources: Institute for Policy Studies, Reich, Just Giving 2018]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Wealth taxes failed in Europe
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Wealth taxes failed in Europe]

Most European wealth taxes were riddled with exemptions and had no strong enforcement or exit tax. Switzerland's wealth tax still raises significant revenue. Design matters.

[Sources: OECD 2018, Saez & Zucman]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Workers should negotiate individually
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Workers should negotiate individually]

An individual worker has almost no leverage against a corporation. Collective bargaining exists because the power imbalance is enormous. It's why union members earn more.

[Sources: BLS Union Members 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Raising wages causes inflation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Raising wages causes inflation]

Corporate profits drove about half of price growth in the nonfinancial sector from mid-2020 through 2021, according to EPI. Wages lagged prices for much of that period.

[Sources: EPI 2022]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Price gouging is just supply and demand
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Price gouging is just supply and demand]

Record profits during a crisis show companies used the moment to raise prices beyond their cost increases. Executives openly discussed pricing power on earnings calls.

[Sources: EPI 2022, Groundwork Collaborative]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Social Security is going broke
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Social Security is going broke]

Even after the trust fund is projected to run down around 2034, incoming payroll taxes would still cover about 80% of benefits. Lifting the cap on taxable earnings, about $176,000 in 2025, would close much of the gap.

[Sources: Social Security Trustees 2025]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medicare for All would raise taxes
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medicare for All would raise taxes]

It would replace premiums, deductibles and copays. For most families, the new taxes would be less than what they already pay to insurers.

[Sources: Galvani et al., Lancet 2020, PERI 2018]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Private insurance gives people choice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Private insurance gives people choice]

Insurance plans come with narrow networks. Your employer chooses your plan and you lose it when you lose your job. Single payer would let you see any participating doctor.

[Sources: KFF]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Government can't run anything
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Government can't run anything]

Medicare, Social Security, the interstate highways and public libraries work for hundreds of millions of people. Medicare's administrative costs are lower than most private insurers'.

[Sources: CMS, Commonwealth Fund]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The poor don't pay taxes
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The poor don't pay taxes]

Low-income families pay sales taxes, payroll taxes, and property taxes through rent. In most states, the poorest 20% pay a bigger share of income in state and local taxes than the richest 1%.

[Sources: ITEP, Who Pays? 2024]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Cutting corporate taxes raises wages
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Cutting corporate taxes raises wages]

After the 2017 tax law, the promised average raise of $4,000 or more never showed up. Stock buybacks hit records instead.

[Sources: CRS 2019, S&P Dow Jones Indices]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Free college is unaffordable
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Free college is unaffordable]

Many countries offer free or low-cost public college. The U.S. spends heavily on tax breaks for the wealthy. It's a matter of priorities, not possibility.

[Sources: OECD Education at a Glance]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Borrowers chose to take on student debt
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Borrowers chose to take on student debt]

Teenagers were told college was required for a middle-class life, while tuition rose and grants shrank. They followed the rules. The system changed the price.

[Sources: TICAS, College Board Trends]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Childcare is a family responsibility, not a public one
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Childcare is a family responsibility, not a public one]

We already fund public school from age five. Early childhood is when brains develop most. Countries that fund childcare see more parents working and better outcomes for kids.

[Sources: OECD Family Database, Heckman research]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Paid sick leave hurts business
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Paid sick leave hurts business]

When Connecticut and other places required paid sick leave, studies found little or no harm to employment, and fewer sick people working spreads less illness.

[Sources: CEPR 2014, Pichler & Ziebarth 2017]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Public housing failed
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Public housing failed]

Public housing was underfunded and segregated by design, then capped by the Faircloth Amendment. Where it's funded well, like Vienna, it works for millions.

[Sources: Faircloth Amendment 1998, City of Vienna]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: People don't want to work anymore
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: People don't want to work anymore]

Prime-age employment reached its highest level in over two decades in 2023–2024. People want to work. They want jobs that pay enough to live on.

[Sources: BLS]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Congress members trading stocks is fine
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Congress members trading stocks is fine]

Lawmakers get briefings and write laws that move markets. Even with the 2012 STOCK Act, many have been found late or noncompliant with disclosure. A full ban is supported across party lines.

[Sources: Business Insider, Conflicted Congress, STOCK Act 2012]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The Supreme Court is above politics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The Supreme Court is above politics]

Justices have accepted undisclosed luxury travel and gifts from billionaires with interests in politics, as ProPublica reported in 2023. The Court only adopted an ethics code under pressure, with no enforcement.

[Sources: ProPublica 2023, Supreme Court Code of Conduct 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Police violence is rare
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Police violence is rare]

U.S. police kill more than 1,000 people a year, far more per capita than other wealthy democracies. Black Americans are killed at more than twice the rate of white Americans.

[Sources: Washington Post Fatal Force, Mapping Police Violence]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: What about Black-on-Black crime?
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: What about Black-on-Black crime?]

Most violent crime happens between people who live near each other and know each other. White victims are also mostly harmed by white offenders. Nobody talks about 'white-on-white crime' because it's segregation, not race, at work.

[Sources: Bureau of Justice Statistics]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Voter ID prevents fraud
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Voter ID prevents fraud]

In-person impersonation, the only fraud ID can stop, is extremely rare. Millions of eligible citizens lack current government ID, disproportionately elderly, poor and Black voters.

[Sources: Levitt 2014, Brennan Center]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Mail-in voting is full of fraud
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Mail-in voting is full of fraud]

States like Utah, Colorado and Washington have voted mostly by mail for years with very little fraud. Ballots are tracked and signatures verified.

[Sources: Brennan Center, Heritage Foundation fraud database (small numbers)]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The drug war keeps communities safe
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The drug war keeps communities safe]

Fifty years of drug war led to mass incarceration and record overdose deaths. Treatment, naloxone and harm reduction save lives.

[Sources: CDC NCHS, Drug Policy Alliance]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Prisons rehabilitate people
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Prisons rehabilitate people]

About two-thirds of people released from state prison are rearrested within three years. Prisons offer little education or job training and release people with almost nothing.

[Sources: Bureau of Justice Statistics]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Prison labor teaches job skills
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Prison labor teaches job skills]

Incarcerated workers often earn pennies an hour, can't unionize, and face punishment for refusing work. Most prison jobs don't lead to employment after release.

[Sources: Prison Policy Initiative 2017, ACLU 2022]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Mass incarceration made us safer
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Mass incarceration made us safer]

Incarceration has steep diminishing returns. The U.S. locks up far more people than peer countries without being safer. Many states cut prison populations while crime kept falling.

[Sources: Brennan Center 2015, The Sentencing Project]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Natural gas is a clean bridge fuel
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Natural gas is a clean bridge fuel]

Methane traps about 80 times more heat than CO2 over 20 years. With leaks from wells and pipelines, gas can be nearly as bad for the climate as coal in the near term.

[Sources: IPCC AR6, Alvarez et al., Science 2018]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The Green New Deal would cost $93 trillion
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The Green New Deal would cost $93 trillion]

That figure came from a conservative think tank estimate that included policies not in the resolution, like guaranteed jobs. And it ignored the trillions climate disasters are already costing us.

[Sources: American Action Forum 2019, NOAA NCEI]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Fossil fuel companies are part of the climate solution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Fossil fuel companies are part of the climate solution]

Shell and BP scaled back their climate targets as profits soared. Exxon's own scientists predicted warming decades ago while the company funded doubt.

[Sources: Company statements 2023–2024, Supran et al., Science 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Drug companies need high prices to fund innovation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Drug companies need high prices to fund innovation]

NIH funding contributed to research behind every one of the 210 new drugs approved from 2010 to 2016. Taxpayers fund much of the science, and big drugmakers spend heavily on buybacks and dividends.

[Sources: Cleghorn et al., PNAS 2018]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Taxing the rich won't raise much money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Taxing the rich won't raise much money]

The Treasury estimated the top 1% fail to pay about $163 billion in owed taxes each year. Ending stepped-up basis and taxing wealth could raise trillions over a decade.

[Sources: U.S. Treasury 2021, Saez & Zucman]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Union decline happened naturally
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Union decline happened naturally]

Union decline followed policy choices: weak labor law enforcement, Taft-Hartley restrictions and aggressive union busting. Employers are charged with illegally firing workers in about 1 in 5 union campaigns.

[Sources: EPI 2019]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Automation, not bosses, is why wages are stagnant
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Automation, not bosses, is why wages are stagnant]

Countries with similar technology but stronger unions and labor laws saw wages grow more. Productivity rose about 65% from 1979 to 2019 while typical pay rose about 18%. The machines didn't take the gains. The owners did.

[Sources: EPI, OECD]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: America has the highest standard of living
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: America has the highest standard of living]

Americans live shorter lives than people in other wealthy countries and face higher medical debt, child poverty and maternal mortality. Averages hide how many people are struggling.

[Sources: CDC NCHS, OECD, UNICEF]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Child poverty is already low
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Child poverty is already low]

Child poverty more than doubled from a record low of 5.2% in 2021 to 12.4% in 2022 after the expanded Child Tax Credit expired. We know how to fix it.

[Sources: Census Supplemental Poverty Measure]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: SNAP fraud is rampant
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: SNAP fraud is rampant]

USDA estimated SNAP benefit trafficking at about 1.5 cents per benefit dollar. That's tiny next to the hundreds of billions in unpaid taxes each year.

[Sources: USDA FNS, IRS tax gap 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Medicaid expansion costs too much
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Medicaid expansion costs too much]

Federal funds cover 90% of expansion costs. Studies found expansion saved lives, with mortality among near-elderly low-income adults falling about 9%.

[Sources: KFF, Miller et al., QJE 2021]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Healthcare should be earned
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Healthcare should be earned]

Nobody earns cancer or a car crash. Every other wealthy country treats healthcare as a right, and they spend less and live longer.

[Sources: OECD Health Statistics]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Public schools are failing, so vouchers are better
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Public schools are failing, so vouchers are better]

In Louisiana, students who used vouchers saw significant drops in math scores. Vouchers drain funding from public schools that serve most kids.

[Sources: Abdulkadiroglu, Pathak & Walters 2018]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Socialism means Venezuela
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Socialism means Venezuela]

Democratic socialists point to Nordic-style policies like universal healthcare, strong unions and free college, combined with democracy and civil liberties. Those countries rank among the happiest and freest in the world.

[Sources: World Happiness Report, Freedom House]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Worker co-ops can't compete
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Worker co-ops can't compete]

Mondragon in Spain employs tens of thousands of worker-members, and research finds co-ops are about as productive as conventional firms and often more stable in downturns.

[Sources: Mondragon Corporation, Pérotin, Co-operatives UK 2016]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: High rent is caused by too much regulation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: High rent is caused by too much regulation]

Restrictive zoning does limit supply, and we should end exclusionary zoning. But the market still won't build homes for the lowest earners. That takes public and social housing.

[Sources: JCHS 2024, NLIHC]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Tipped workers make good money
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Tipped workers make good money]

The federal tipped minimum wage is $2.13 an hour, unchanged since 1991. In states with one fair wage for everyone, like California, restaurant jobs have continued to grow.

[Sources: DOL, One Fair Wage / BLS data]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: The gender pay gap is a myth
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: The gender pay gap is a myth]

Women working full-time, year-round earned about 83 cents for every dollar paid to men in 2023. Part of the gap reflects occupational segregation and the motherhood penalty, which are themselves products of discrimination.

[Sources: Census 2023, Goldin, Nobel lecture 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Noncompetes protect business secrets
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Noncompetes protect business secrets]

Roughly one in five workers is bound by a noncompete, including low-wage workers with no trade secrets. They mostly suppress wages and job mobility.

[Sources: FTC 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: OSHA regulations are excessive
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: OSHA regulations are excessive]

More than 5,000 workers die on the job each year, and there's still no federal heat standard. Child labor violations rose 88% from 2019 to 2023. The problem is too little enforcement, not too much.

[Sources: BLS CFOI, DOL 2023]

title: Karl Counter-Argument: Private equity makes businesses more efficient
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Claim: Private equity makes businesses more efficient]

Private equity ownership of nursing homes was linked to about an 11% rise in short-term patient mortality. 'Efficiency' often means cutting staff and loading companies with debt.

[Sources: Gupta et al., NBER 2021]
